cues.text: Good afternoon. May I speak to Emma’s parent?
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Afternoon. I’m her father. Who am I speaking to?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: This is Emma’s teacher Jane Carson calling from the Art Centre.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I’m just calling to talk about her drama class at the centre.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Oh, thank you for calling. How’s Emma doing in drama class?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: You know she just transferred here last month, unlike the others in her class who have been taking the course the whole semester since June.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: So I’m a bit worried that she might not fit in so well.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: There’s no need to worry. She exhibits a strong performance in her drama class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Is that so?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Yes. She didn’t adapt to the new environment as quickly as I originally expected, and seemed a bit shy at first.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: But a few days later, she made a couple of friends and became more talkative and also more involved in class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Emma really is a role model for others, because she has always been an active participant
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: She voices her own ideas and is very creative.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I didn’t expect that. But I can tell that she really enjoys the course,
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: because she’s been talking about it at home frequently these past few weeks.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: That’s great to hear. Interest is always the best teacher.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I also have to inform you that there’s been an adjustment in the timetable of the drama class next term.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Why is that?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: It’s not that the music room that we currently use isn’t available.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: As there are too many enrolling for the coming semester, increased class size means that space is limited to house the whole class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Also the new classroom we use is not available during the current timeframe, so I’m afraid we have to change the time for it.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I see. So when would it be?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: As you know, the current class begins at three fifteen.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: But the new time of thedrama class would be a quarter to five.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I’m afraid I have errands to run during that time.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: On the other campus the class still begins at three fifteen, but for the campus Emma goes to, it is the only time available for drama class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Oh. I see. I have to make adjustments to my chore schedule then. No problem.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Miss Carson, I’m thinking about signing Emma up for another art course.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: I’m thinking about dance class.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Dance class is a popular course here, a great choice for a child to shape up and have fun.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: But unfortunately, it is over-subscribed at the moment.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: I have to put you on the waiting list.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: That’s too bad. What else can I choose from then? Could you give me some advice?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Sure. Emma could take singing class as well. This would improve her musicality.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Sounds good. When is that?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: It is held every Friday evening.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: That’s too bad.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Emma already has a swimming class earlier that evening.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: It will be too late for her to come home if she takes this course.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: There is also a vocal course available.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Emma’s got a great voice, I’m sure she’ll stand out in the class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Tell me about it.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: The vocal course starts at 4.30 pm every Tuesday.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: It isn’t fully booked yet. Great teacher, experienced and beloved by students.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: The price is a bit higher though.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: How much is it?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: It’s 110 dollars.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Oh, that’s too much, way over our budget.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: We have to cover the extra cost if we choose it.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Or maybe Emma could take music class.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: What is it about? Learning about songs and musicals?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Well, the students have the opportunity to play different instruments like the piano, drum and so on.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: They can also learn how to write music under professional guidance.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: That’s exactly what Emma is eager to learn. How much would it cost?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: It was 63 dollars last term.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: But this term it is 85 dollars, 22 dollars more than the original price.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: We can afford that. When does the course begin?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: The course starts on September 7th.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Can we start one week later, on September 14th?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: My daughter will be on a trip to France with her Mom on the 7th.
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: No problem. And the teacher for the class is Jamal Curtis.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Just contact him if you have any further questions regarding the course.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Jamal Curtis? How do you spell Curtis?
cues.speaker: Father

cues.text: Oh, it’s C-U-R-T-I-S.
cues.speaker: Teacher

cues.text: Thank you.
cues.speaker: Father
